text:
Maya Patel: Heads up — after the kernel-selector rollout (canary -> prod) we're seeing a ~12% p95 increase on host-side request latency. Traces point to a higher number of writev syscalls from the proxy layer and more small streaming frames. https://traces.internal/r/4187654321

perf-bot: Alert: host-proxy writev_count increased by +2.9/write per req, kvcache miss rate +11.7% on canary group.

Arjun Singh: Repro steps? which commit rolled? any config changes to batching heuristics or frame coalescing?

Maya Patel: Commit: github.com/redwood/runtime@c4f9a7d - kernel-selector: prefer-mini-batch-path when estimated_token_rate < 500. Also default batch_hint changed from 8 -> 4 in the same PR. Rolled to 30% yesterday.

Priya Chen: Quick profile dump from canary host (sampled):
```
# strace snippet (summarized)
writev(...)= 1  # small frame (~256B)
writev(...)= 1  # small frame (~320B)
writev(...)= 1  # small frame (~128B)
# prior to rollout these were coalesced into single larger writev
```
KV cache stats: hit_rate dropped 87.3% -> 76.1% for short-ttl keys (prefix cache). CPU softirq up 3%.

Tom Baker: Sounds like the smaller batch_hint causes earlier flushes -> more fragments -> more writev ops and worse KV locality. Kernel selector choosing mini-batch path increases per-request RPCs (more framing).

Arjun Singh: Can we confirm whether kernel-selector's token-rate heuristic misestimates for bursty traffic? If it flips to mini-batch for short requests we lose prefix sharing in KV cache.

Priya Chen: I ran a quick A/B: forcing batch_hint=8 on canary drops writev_count back to baseline and recovers p95. Patch to verify:
```
# temp override
kernel_selector:
  prefer_mini_batch: false
  batch_hint: 8
```

Maya Patel: Good. Action plan? revert config or roll back selector? We need a short-term mitigation and a followup fix.

Tom Baker: Short-term: push config override to canary group (batch_hint=8), and flip selector to conservative mode (prefer_mini_batch=false). Medium-term: update selector to consider kvcache_hotness and frame coalescing cost in its decision function.

Arjun Singh: I'll open a bisect PR to isolate when frame coalescing changed vs when selector threshold changed. Also propose adding a synthetic workload to exercise short bursts to measure estimated_token_rate accuracy.

Maya Patel: I'll push the config override now and schedule a perf run. If p95 recovers within 30m we'll keep and iterate on selector cost model.

perf-bot: Deploy note: override applied to canary pool at 4187654350 by maya. Monitoring TTL 45m.

Priya Chen: Follow-ups: add telemetry for "selector_decision_reason" in traces, and emit kvcache prefix hit distribution per decision-mode. That will let us quantify cost tradeoffs.

Maya Patel: Thanks — keeping thread open for rollback results. If p95 doesn't fall back, we'll roll the canary back to previous commit.

Tom Baker: Also add a microbenchmark: 100K short requests (avg 16 tokens) to validate selector's token-rate estimator and verify kernel path choices.

Maya Patel: Noted. Will report back in ~40m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
